chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the ghusl of Friday, and he said: “It is a sunnah (prophetic tradition) in travel and residence, except when the traveler fears the cold for himself.”

key_terms.اَلْجُمُعَةِ: Friday, referring here to the Friday ghusl
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a recommended prophetic practice, not an obligatory act

ai.seo_question: Is Friday ghusl recommended for a traveler as well as a resident?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Friday ghusl is a sunnah (prophetic tradition) whether one is traveling or resident. An exception is made for the traveler when he fears harm from the cold, indicating consideration of hardship in ritual practice.
